newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields end 21 basis points higher.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields end 21 basis points higher.

text.p: Swedish bond yields rose further on Tuesday while shorter maturities shed a few basis points.
Dealers said the longer end continued to be driven by 'stop-loss' orders.
"Many trading account are in for short positions instead of longer ones and when yields have increased enough others follow suit," one dealer said.
The ten-year bond yield climbed 21 basis points to 7.35 percent and the spread between Swedish and German long yields increased 14 basis points to 153.

"We are increasing the spread against everyone and we have never seen such a strong movement. The market is very volatile, the fear governs and the focus is only set on the proper position," one dealer said.
Since the liquidity had to go somewhere the shorter maturities slid. Six-month T-bill rates were down one basis point to 4.33 percent.
Meanwhile the crown weakened to 4.6000 against the generally stronger mark from 4.5815 late on Monday.
